record.title: Species record
record.description: One file per term, named for the term's slug. Every audience reads this file: the README, the site, and the issue form a contributor fills in.

issue.name: New species
issue.description: Propose a creature for the Civic Bestiary
issue.intro: Thanks for proposing a term. Fill in what you can - the maintainers handle placement, cross-references, and the final edit. One proposal per issue, please.
issue.outro: A proposal lands as a record under `data/species/` once the writing holds up. The bar is not novelty, it is use: the term should name something a reader recognises and has no word for yet.

fields.label: Term
fields.hint: The portmanteau, spelled the way it should be listed. Title case, no quotes.

fields.label: Order
fields.hint: Which order the creature keeps. The maintainers will move it if it belongs elsewhere.

fields.label: Part of speech
fields.hint: What the term is grammatically. Most are nouns.

fields.label: Pronunciation
fields.hint: IPA between slashes. Approximate is fine.

fields.label: Etymology
fields.hint: Where the word came from, in one line. Name both parents if it is a blend.

fields.label: Range
fields.hint: Where you meet it. Concrete places, not abstractions - truck beds, county fairs, a specific comment section.
fields.example: Truck beds, county fairs, and the comment section under any local news post.

fields.label: Call
fields.hint: The thing it says. A short quotation, ideally something you have actually heard.

fields.label: Field marks
fields.hint: How you recognise it at a distance. Three is the house number; one per line.
fields.example: Flag decal on a leased vehicle

fields.label: Senses
fields.hint: Two definitions: the creature, then the pattern it runs. Full sentences, one per line. The first sense becomes the page description, so make it stand alone.
fields.example: A citizen who performs patriotism as a shield while undermining the civic obligations it claims to honour.

fields.label: Example
fields.hint: One sentence in the wild, with the term in bold. Wrap the quotation in *asterisks*; the README renders it as an aside.
fields.example: *"He wrapped himself in the flag at every rally, yet his refusal to respect basic civic responsibilities showed he was more of a **playtriot** than a true patriot."*

fields.label: Easily confused with
fields.hint: Existing terms it could be mistaken for, and the one thing that tells them apart. Optional at proposal time - the maintainers add twins when the confusion is real.
fields.example: LARPtarian - both dress the part; the playtriot buys the flag, the LARPtarian buys the surplus rifle.

fields.label: Cross-references
fields.hint: Two or three existing terms this one belongs beside. The graph must stay connected, so every term needs at least one inbound reference.

fields.label: Position in order
fields.hint: Where the entry sits inside its order. Appending means one past the current highest.
